To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The inference of structure in images can be achieved by using a multi-local spatial filter bank, with the filter responses combined to give confidence measures in a Bayesian framework.”

we present a method for inferring the presence of junctions and corners in images using epistemic probability theory, and that we show a relationship between Fourier domain and spatial domain models of filtering.

1) the multi-local quadrature filters are able to detect the corners in the image, 2) the multi-local spatial separation is able to classify the image structure into line end points, and 3) the Fourier domain model is able to detect the line end points in the image.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new theory of image structure and its implementation in an image processing algorithm.
the inference of image structure, and the use of multi-local filters for the detection of corners, edges and junctions.
the use of Fourier analysis in the spatial domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of both Fourier and spatial domain filters is required to achieve a complete description of image structure.
the spatial domain model is a more accurate representation of the Fourier domain model.
a multi-local filter approach is more robust than a band of filters approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to infer the structure of images by using a multi-local quadrature filter approach.
a combination of multi-local spatial and frequency domain filtering is necessary for a complete characterization of the image.
we have demonstrated that the Fourier domain is a powerful means of inferring structure in images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of multi-local quadrature filters is a viable alternative to Gabor filters in corner detection.
the use of a band of filters can provide more information than a single filter.
the spatial domain is a powerful tool for the analysis of images.
